question: What freshwater-fish information does the official MCTEP Segment 5 EIS report for Ylang-Yang River and Maalimango Creek, and can its taxa be assigned to either named waterbody?

source.title: Environmental Impact Statement (EIS): Manila-Cavite Toll Expressway Project (MCTEP) Segment 5, Volume 1 Main Report (revised 20 July 2019)
relevantLocators: Figure 2.53, Freshwater Ecology Sampling Site Map, printed page 2-80
Section 2.2.4.3 Fish and Tables 2.25-2.26, printed page 2-82
source.sourceDescribedProjectArea: Cavite City and municipalities of Kawit, Noveleta, Rosario, and Tanza, Cavite, according to the official EIA public-comment listing. This project-area description is not a site-to-municipality crosswalk.

samplingSites.linkType: source-named station only; station coordinates and reach limits not supplied in the reviewed fish section
source-named station only; not merged with the separately recorded Maalimango River; station coordinates and reach limits not supplied in the reviewed fish section

findings.siteTaxonAllocation: The Figure 2.53 map names two freshwater sampling sites, but Table 2.25 pools fish results for Ylang-Yang River and Maalimango Creek. No species-by-site, station, day/night, or individual capture crosswalk is shown. None of the pooled taxa is assigned to either site separately.
findings.methods: The EIS says modified backpack electrofishing was used at each survey station for about one hour over a 100 m reach; samples were preserved on ice and identified in a laboratory to the lowest possible taxon using Froese and Pauly (2011). The narrative says day and night sampling were combined and describes catch per hour. The stated overall 12-hour effort is not reconciled with the visible station-level description.

sourceTableIntegrity.discrepancy: The five species/genus rows sum to 126, whereas the table mean-density total and narrative say 127. The prose also says “eight (5)” freshwater fish species representing “seven (5)” families, while the displayed table lists five taxa in five families. These inconsistencies are retained unresolved; family subtotal rows duplicate the taxon counts and are not added again.

findings.collectionDate: No fish collection date was found in the reviewed section. Nearby water-quality dates are not transferred to the fish sampling.
findings.coordinates: No station coordinates or exact sampling reach geometry were supplied in the reviewed map/section; no coordinates were digitized.
findings.sourceDietAndStatusColumns: Table 2.26 contains source-era status and feeding labels with citations to Froese and Pauly (2011) and IUCN Red List version 2017.2. These secondary, dated labels are not adopted as current taxonomic, native/introduced, conservation, or local natural-diet claims for Bangwit.

limitations: The evidence is historical EIS baseline information, not a present-day occurrence record, complete local inventory, population estimate, or fishery catchability result.
The map identifies two station names, but the fish table is pooled; there is no defensible taxon assignment to Ylang-Yang River versus Maalimango Creek.
The original fish collection dates, voucher/catalog numbers, exact coordinates, and item-specific data reuse license were not established.

The direct file retrieval in this workspace returned a Cloudflare challenge page rather than PDF bytes. The official PDF text and map were reviewed through the web document reader; no local PDF copy or file hash is claimed.
The EIS project footprint is not waterbody geometry, municipal-water boundary, or fishing-access guidance.

disposition.reason: The official EIS exposes useful historical freshwater fish research context and two named sampling sites, but the taxon table is pooled and internally inconsistent. Record the source for research discovery only; retain both waterbody identities separately and admit no species-level locality assertion or public row.

nextAction: Seek an independently reviewable station-to-taxon crosswalk, fish sampling dates, voucher/identification details, and item-specific reuse terms for the EIS if they exist. Continue independent CALABARZON freshwater and marine source review in parallel; do not infer a site-level species checklist from the pooled table.
